Five top-level bullets, two steps. Bullets 1 to 4 are ONE conversation, not four visits: 2 and 3 are the dress-up scene and Naja's demand that you change clothes, and 4 is the warning that you must speak to her AGAIN once changed or the palace cutscene never fires. One NPC, one marker, and readiness looks ahead across it anyway. Bullet 5 is the door.

The dress code is the interesting failure and the reason for the flag. The page lists 36 acceptable body pieces, and on top of that ANY gloves, leg armour and boots, and bullet 5 additionally wants your weapons REMOVED. That is a 36-way OR joined to an AND over three more slots joined to a negative. items_alt can express the OR and nothing in the schema can express the rest, so no items are recorded at all and items_partial is set on both steps -- shipping only the body-piece third of that predicate would read 'ready' while the player is still barefoot and armed, which is a confidently wrong answer to a question the page answers plainly. The requirement is also about what is EQUIPPED rather than what is held, which the runtime does not distinguish. Demoted to medium for that alone: both markers are in the right place and the ladder is right, but a step whose real precondition is this large and this invisible will read ready while the player is still going to be turned away at the door.
